messages:
maria: Repro for an offline->online stampede in the Kotlin sample app. When device regains connectivity WorkManager starts ~12 UploadWorkers and OkHttp fires them all. Our AuthInterceptor triggers multiple refreshes and we see a cascade of 401s/429s.

aj: Noted. Which okhttp/retrofit versions? Also paste the client config.

maria: okhttp 4.11.0, retrofit 2.9.0, coroutine call-adapter. Client: 
```kotlin
OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .retryOnConnectionFailure(true)
  .dispatcher(Dispatcher().apply { maxRequests = 64; maxRequestsPerHost = 20 })
  .addInterceptor(AuthInterceptor(tokenProvider))
  .build()
```

maria: Logs: 
```
2026-03-18 18:22:11 UploadWorker: network available, launching 12 workers
2026-03-18 18:22:11 AuthInterceptor: token expired, refreshing
2026-03-18 18:22:11 AuthInterceptor: token expired, refreshing
2026-03-18 18:22:12 Retrofit: 401 Unauthorized
2026-03-18 18:22:12 Retrofit: 429 Too Many Requests
```

sophia: Classic stampede. Two orthogonal fixes: single-flight token refresh and reduce Concurrency in sample. Use a Deferred singleflight or Mutex + withLock to avoid blocking thread pools.

aj: Also set retryOnConnectionFailure(false) in sample apps and implement explicit backoff in workers. OkHttp's auto retry can re-submit on flappy networks which makes bursts worse.

tim: Watch coroutine cancellation -> OkHttp call parity. If a Worker cancels but the adapter doesn't cancel the underlying Call, you can end up with duplicate inflight network work. Ensure the CallAdapter cancels call on coroutine cancellation. We had a bug where calls continued after worker cancellation.

maria: For singleflight we tried AtomicReference<Deferred<Token>> and it worked in local tests. Example:
```kotlin
private val refreshRef = AtomicReference<Deferred<Token>?>(null)
suspend fun singleflightRefresh(): Token {
  refreshRef.get()?.let { return it.await() }
  val d = CoroutineScope(Dispatchers.IO).async(start = LAZY) { tokenProvider.refresh() }
  if (!refreshRef.compareAndSet(null, d)) return refreshRef.get()!!.await()
  try { d.start(); return d.await() } finally { refreshRef.set(null) }
}
```

sophia: Nice. For sample app PR I'll: (1) add AggregatorWorker draining a bounded queue, (2) default maxRequestsPerHost=4, (3) default retryOnConnectionFailure=false, (4) replace interceptor with Deferred singleflight, (5) add integration test that simulates offline->online and asserts only 1 refresh call.

aj: Add a note in README about WorkManager semantics (ExistingWorkPolicy vs enqueuing many unique works) and about adapter cancellation. That helps DX.

maria: Thanks — I'll run the PR against Pixel 7 and an old Android 10 device to confirm behavior under low memory. Will also test network flaps with emulator settings.

sophia: If you see dispatcher queue growth again, please paste dispatcher.runningCallsCount and dispatcher.queuedCalls into logs before starting large batches. That helps triage.

maria: Will do. Appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:
